cards.title: GNPS Program 7: Paediatric Nursing
cards.body: Global Nursing Professional Series — Level 3

cards.title: Welcome to Level 3
cards.body: At Level 3, you become a Global Nursing Professional — going beyond bedside care to lead paediatric safety, strengthen child-protection systems, and advocate for equitable, high-quality services.

bullets.label: This level develops advanced capability in:
Digital child health and workforce development
Lead child-centred paediatric services and strengthen deterioration recognition systems.
Design and evaluate QI initiatives; analyse patterns of preventable child harm.
Promote safeguarding, children's rights and integrated care for chronic conditions.
Use digital child-health technologies responsibly and contribute to global child-health equity.

cards.title: Why This Learning Matters
cards.body: Preventable harm in children can arise from delayed recognition, incorrect dosing, fragmented care, communication barriers, or failure to identify abuse and neglect.

bullets.label: Global Nursing Professionals understand these
bullets.text: Global Nursing Professionals understand these system connections and lead practical, measurable improvement for every child in their care.

cards.title: Your Learning Goal
cards.body: Lead. Improve. Advocate.

bullets.label: By completing Level 3, you will be prepared to
bullets.text: By completing Level 3, you will be prepared to lead paediatric quality and safety initiatives, use evidence and data to strengthen services, support colleagues, and contribute to healthier childhoods — locally and globally.

bullets.label: Drive safety and improvement across paediatric services
Use data and research to strengthen outcomes
Advocate for equitable child health locally and worldwide

cards.title: SECTION 1
cards.body: Leading Child- and Family-Centred Paediatric Services

bullets.label: Leadership in paediatric care means creating
bullets.text: Leadership in paediatric care means creating services that are safe, developmentally appropriate, respectful and responsive to children and families. Global Nursing Professionals model excellent practice and strengthen team capability.

bullets.label: Describe leadership responsibilities in paediatric services
Support staff competence and psychological safety

cards.title: Core Concepts: Section 1
cards.body: Child- & Family-Centred Leadership

bullets.label: Care that respects developmental needs, family
bullets.text: Care that respects developmental needs, family expertise, privacy and participation. Services adapt to children — not the other way around.

bullets.label: Staff must feel confident to raise concerns,
bullets.text: Staff must feel confident to raise concerns, question doses and seek help without fear — enabling early escalation and error prevention.

bullets.label: Regular education and simulation build response
bullets.text: Regular education and simulation build response capability for paediatric emergencies, medication calculations and safeguarding situations.

bullets.label: Children have rights to safety, dignity,
bullets.text: Children have rights to safety, dignity, information and participation. Leaders embed these rights in everyday policies and practice.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Section 1
cards.body: Junior nurses on a paediatric unit hesitated to challenge unusual medication doses — a serious patient safety risk.

bullets.label: The Response: Leaders introduced dose-check
bullets.text: The Response: Leaders introduced dose-check huddles, simulation training and a clear escalation pathway. Staff confidence increased and near misses were identified earlier.

bullets.label: More near misses caught; confidence improved

cards.title: SECTION 2
cards.body: Systems for Paediatric Safety and Deterioration

bullets.label: Paediatric safety systems must account for
bullets.text: Paediatric safety systems must account for rapid physiological change, weight-based treatment and dependence on caregivers. Effective systems link observation, escalation, emergency response and learning.

cards.title: Core Concepts: Section 2
cards.body: Early Warning & Escalation

bullets.label: Paediatric early warning tools support
bullets.text: Paediatric early warning tools support recognition — effectiveness depends on accurate observations and timely response to scores and clinical concern.

bullets.label: Wrong weight, concentration, decimal errors and
bullets.text: Wrong weight, concentration, decimal errors and adult formulations cause severe harm. Standard concentrations and dose-range checks reduce risk.

bullets.label: Noise, interruption, fatigue and unclear
bullets.text: Noise, interruption, fatigue and unclear responsibility contribute to error. System redesign is stronger than relying on reminders alone.

bullets.label: Reviews should involve frontline staff and
bullets.text: Reviews should involve frontline staff and families, examining clinical, communication and system factors to prevent recurrence.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Section 2
cards.body: A review of paediatric infusion incidents identified inconsistent concentration charts and frequent interruptions during medication preparation.

bullets.label: Standardised concentration charts across all wards
Redesigned preparation areas to reduce interruptions
Result: Measurable reduction in infusion-related incidents and improved staff confidence.

cards.title: SECTION 3
cards.body: Quality Improvement, Safeguarding and Integrated Care

bullets.label: Global Nursing Professionals use data to
bullets.text: Global Nursing Professionals use data to improve paediatric outcomes and strengthen systems that protect children. Improvement should include clinical outcomes, family experience, equity and safeguarding.

bullets.label: Use paediatric data to identify priorities
Promote integrated care for complex needs

cards.title: Clinical Example: Section 3
cards.body: Reducing Asthma Readmissions

bullets.label: A service identified frequent asthma
bullets.text: A service identified frequent asthma readmissions among children from one disadvantaged area. The improvement team introduced inhaler teaching, school action plans, community follow-up and access support.

bullets.label: Data reveals readmission cluster in one area
Inhaler teaching, school plans, community support

cards.title: SECTION 4
cards.body: Digital Child Health and Global Paediatric Practice

bullets.label: Digital records, telehealth, remote monitoring
bullets.text: Digital records, telehealth, remote monitoring and decision support can improve paediatric care — but may also create privacy, access and automation risks.

bullets.label: Global Nursing Professionals use technology critically and advocate for equitable child health.
Evaluate digital technologies in paediatric care
Promote safe virtual and remote care

cards.title: Core Concepts: Section 4
cards.body: Digital Paediatric Records

bullets.label: Shared records improve continuity — but
bullets.text: Shared records improve continuity — but incorrect weight, copied data or outdated medication must be verified. Critical information always needs checking.

bullets.label: Virtual care supports chronic disease and rural
bullets.text: Virtual care supports chronic disease and rural families — provided clear escalation pathways and alternatives for limited digital access exist.

bullets.label: Digital systems must protect sensitive
bullets.text: Digital systems must protect sensitive adolescent information while supporting safe communication with caregivers in line with law and policy.

bullets.label: Improving child health requires vaccination,
bullets.text: Improving child health requires vaccination, nutrition, injury prevention, clean environments and accessible primary care — adapted to local culture and resources.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Section 4
cards.body: Telehealth for Children with Diabetes

bullets.label: A regional service introduced telehealth for
bullets.text: A regional service introduced telehealth for children with diabetes. Leaders recognised that digital care could widen inequality if not carefully designed.

bullets.label: Equipment loans for families without devices
Community alternatives for those without reliable internet
Digital innovation must never leave vulnerable families behind.

cards.title: The GNPS Learning Pathway
cards.body: Level 1 — Qualified Nurse

bullets.label: Build strong foundations in child development, assessment, common illness and safety.
Manage complex paediatric care, safeguarding and international practice expectations.
Lead quality, safety, equity and innovation in child and family health services.

cards.title: Programme Complete — What You Have Achieved
cards.body: By completing GNPS Program 7 – Level 3, you have developed the advanced perspective of a Global Nursing Professional. You are prepared to:

bullets.label: Drive paediatric safety and quality initiatives at service level
Strengthen systems that protect children and uphold their rights
Support evidence-based innovation and responsible digital care
Champion equitable child health locally and globally

cards.title: Section 1: Leading Child- and Family-Centred Paediatric Services
cards.body: Introduction

bullets.label: Leadership in paediatric care means creating
bullets.text: Leadership in paediatric care means creating services that are safe, developmentally appropriate, respectful and responsive to children and families.

bullets.label: Global Nursing Professionals model excellent
bullets.text: Global Nursing Professionals model excellent practice and strengthen team capability — setting the standard for every interaction with a child and their family.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you should be able to:

bullets.label: Articulate the role of the nurse leader in paediatric services.
Champion approaches that engage and respect families as partners.
Foster psychological safety and ongoing professional development.
Embed rights-based principles into policies and everyday practice.

cards.title: Child- and Family-Centred Leadership
cards.body: Effective paediatric leaders ensure that care respects developmental needs, family expertise, privacy and participation. Services must adapt to children — not the other way around.

bullets.label: Service routines should flex around the child, not expect children to conform to adult systems.

cards.title: Psychological Safety in the Paediatric Team
cards.body: Speak Up Without Fear

bullets.label: Staff must feel confident raising concerns,
bullets.text: Staff must feel confident raising concerns, questioning doses and requesting support — without risk of humiliation or blame.

bullets.label: A psychologically safe environment means concerns surface earlier, reducing the risk of clinical deterioration.
Leaders actively model approachability, respond to concerns constructively, and reward speaking up.

cards.title: Building Competence Through Simulation
cards.body: Why Simulation Matters

bullets.label: Regular education and simulation strengthen the
bullets.text: Regular education and simulation strengthen the team's ability to respond to paediatric emergencies, perform accurate medication calculations, and manage safeguarding situations confidently.

cards.title: Advocating for Children's Rights
cards.body: 🛡️ Safety

bullets.label: Every child has the right to care that protects them from harm and unnecessary risk.
Children and families must receive clear, age-appropriate explanations of care and decisions.
Children's voices and family perspectives are actively included in care planning.
All interactions uphold the child's sense of worth, privacy and identity.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Medication Safety on the Ward
cards.body: The Problem

bullets.label: Junior nurses on a paediatric unit hesitated to challenge unusual medication doses — a significant patient safety risk.
Introduced dose-check huddles at the start of each shift
Implemented simulation scenarios around medication errors
Created a clear, blameless escalation pathway

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Design Around Children

bullets.label: Services must be structured around children's developmental, emotional and social needs — not adult convenience.
Cultivate a culture where raising concerns is expected, welcomed and never penalised.
Use regular, realistic simulation to sharpen clinical skills and reduce anxiety in high-stakes situations.
Integrate rights-based principles into every policy, protocol and everyday clinical interaction.

cards.title: Your Next Step in Paediatric Leadership
cards.body: Lead with knowledge. Care with purpose.

bullets.label: Continue building your expertise through the
bullets.text: Continue building your expertise through the GNPS programme — designed to prepare internationally qualified nurses for excellence in global clinical practice and NCLEX success.

bullets.label: SECTION 2: SYSTEMS FOR PAEDIATRIC SAFETY AND DETERIORATION

cards.title: Introduction
cards.body: Paediatric safety systems must account for three defining features of child healthcare:

bullets.label: Effective systems link observation, escalation, emergency response and learning into a single, continuous loop.
Children deteriorate quickly — detection must be proactive.
Every dose, fluid, and intervention is calculated individually.
Families are integral to observation and safety.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you should be able to:

bullets.label: Paediatric deterioration systems and early warning tools
Medication and communication risks specific to children
Learning reviews to prevent recurrence of incidents

cards.title: Core Concept 1: Early Warning and Escalation
cards.body: What Are Paediatric Early Warning Tools?

bullets.label: Structured scoring systems (e.g. PEWS) assign
bullets.text: Structured scoring systems (e.g. PEWS) assign values to vital signs and clinical observations to identify children at risk of deterioration before a crisis occurs.

bullets.label: Effectiveness depends on accurate observations and timely response — to both the score and clinical concern.
Scores must trigger a defined escalation response
Clinical concern should always override a reassuring score

cards.title: Core Concept 2: Medication-System Risks
cards.body: Paediatric medication errors can cause severe, sometimes fatal harm. Understanding where risks arise is the first step to preventing them.

bullets.label: Estimated or unverified weights lead to systematic over- or under-dosing
Variable drug concentrations create confusion at the point of administration
A misplaced decimal point can result in a 10-fold dosing error
Using adult preparations in children increases risk significantly

cards.title: Reducing Medication Risk: System Solutions
cards.body: Why Systems Beat Reminders

bullets.label: Individual vigilance alone cannot reliably
bullets.text: Individual vigilance alone cannot reliably prevent medication errors. Sustainable safety comes from designing out the opportunity for error:

bullets.label: Electronic dose-range checks provide an independent safety net
Pharmacy integration adds expert verification at source

cards.title: Core Concept 3: Human Factors
cards.body: The environment in which care is delivered directly shapes the likelihood of error. In paediatric settings, several factors compound risk:

bullets.label: Distraction during calculation or drug preparation is a leading contributor to error
Cognitive performance declines significantly during long shifts and overnight working
Infrequent use of specialist paediatric devices increases the risk of misuse
Ambiguity over who acts reduces the speed and reliability of response
System redesign is stronger than reminders alone. Telling staff to be more careful is not a safety strategy.

cards.title: Core Concept 4: Learning Reviews
cards.body: Turning Incidents into Improvement

bullets.label: A high-quality learning review examines three interconnected domains:
Reviews should involve frontline staff and
bullets.text: Reviews should involve frontline staff and families where appropriate — those closest to the event hold the richest insight.

bullets.label: What happened at the bedside? Were observations timely and accurate?
Was critical information shared clearly between team members and families?
Did processes, equipment or staffing contribute to the outcome?

cards.title: Clinical Example: Infusion Incident Review
cards.body: A review of paediatric infusion incidents at a hospital uncovers two root causes. Here is how the team responded:

bullets.label: This example illustrates a key principle:
bullets.text: This example illustrates a key principle: identify the system failure, redesign the system, then verify the fix works. Isolated staff training alone would not have solved either root cause.

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: 🔗 Link Tools to Response

bullets.label: Deterioration tools only protect patients when connected to a reliable, practised escalation pathway
Consistent concentrations, weights and processes remove the conditions in which errors thrive
Build systems around normal human limitations — fatigue, distraction and cognitive load are predictable
Turn every incident into a measurable, system-level improvement — not just a reminder
NCLEX Focus: Questions on paediatric safety
bullets.text: NCLEX Focus: Questions on paediatric safety frequently test priority setting, dosage calculation, and escalation decision-making. Connect these concepts to your clinical reasoning.

bullets.label: SECTION 3: QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, SAFEGUARDING AND INTEGRATED CARE

cards.title: Introduction
cards.body: Why Quality Improvement Matters in Paediatrics

bullets.label: Global Nursing Professionals use data to
bullets.text: Global Nursing Professionals use data to improve paediatric outcomes and strengthen systems that protect children. Effective improvement must address:

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Identify priorities using outcome and process data
Use quality-improvement frameworks in clinical practice
Support systems that protect children early
Coordinate care for children with complex needs

cards.title: Quality Priorities in Paediatric Care
cards.body: Common areas requiring focused improvement across paediatric services:

bullets.label: Reducing preventable hospital readmissions through better discharge planning and community follow-up
Minimising errors in prescribing, dispensing and administration for paediatric patients
Implementing evidence-based prevention strategies to reduce HAI rates in children's wards
Ensuring timely, clear information for families — particularly around escalation and care planning

cards.title: Safeguarding Systems
cards.body: Building Robust Child Protection Frameworks

bullets.label: Effective safeguarding depends on clear structures and shared responsibility. Key components include:
Defined escalation routes for all staff when concern arises
Regular case review involving nursing, medical and social care teams
Mandatory safeguarding training updated regularly for all clinical staff
Strong links enabling early intervention and coordinated response

cards.title: Integrated Care for Complex Needs
cards.body: Children with complex health needs require seamless coordination across multiple services and settings.

bullets.label: No single service can meet all needs alone —
bullets.text: No single service can meet all needs alone — integration across these domains improves outcomes and reduces family burden.

cards.title: Measurement and Equity
cards.body: Looking Beyond Overall Averages

bullets.label: Outcome and process data must be examined
bullets.text: Outcome and process data must be examined across key population groups to uncover unequal care that aggregate figures may hide.

bullets.label: Age group — neonates, infants, school-age, adolescents
Geography — urban vs. rural, disadvantaged postcodes
Disability status — additional needs and access barriers
Cultural background — language, health literacy, trust
Equity is not optional — it is a core quality standard in paediatric nursing.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Reducing Asthma Readmissions
cards.body: QUALITY IMPROVEMENT IN ACTION

bullets.label: A service identifies a high rate of asthma
bullets.text: A service identifies a high rate of asthma readmissions among children from one disadvantaged area. The QI team responds with a structured improvement plan.

cards.title: The Improvement Plan: Step by Step
cards.body: Identify

bullets.label: High asthma readmissions in disadvantaged area.
Inhaler teaching, school plans, community follow-up.
Track readmissions and family confidence levels.
Readmissions fall and family confidence improves.
This real-world example illustrates how
bullets.text: This real-world example illustrates how targeted, community-sensitive interventions — grounded in data — can deliver measurable improvements in both clinical outcomes and family experience.

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Take these principles into your clinical practice:

bullets.label: Use outcome and process data to pinpoint where improvement is needed before acting
Patient and family feedback is essential evidence — not an optional extra
Build and maintain partnerships across hospital, community and social care
Disaggregate your data — overall averages can mask significant inequalities
NCLEX Tip: Quality improvement, safeguarding
bullets.text: NCLEX Tip: Quality improvement, safeguarding frameworks and integrated care coordination are high-yield topics for internationally qualified nurse candidates.

cards.title: Digital Child Health & Global Paediatric Practice
cards.body: Global Nursing Professional Series (GNPS) · Program 7 · Level 3 · Section 4

cards.title: Section Overview
cards.body: Why Digital Technology Matters in Paediatric Care

bullets.label: Digital records, telehealth, remote monitoring
bullets.text: Digital records, telehealth, remote monitoring and clinical decision support are reshaping how nurses care for children and families globally.

bullets.label: Yet these tools also introduce privacy risks,
bullets.text: Yet these tools also introduce privacy risks, access inequalities and automation errors that every Global Nursing Professional must recognise and address.

bullets.label: "Every child deserves exceptional care — digital or otherwise."

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: What You Will Be Able to Do

bullets.label: Critically assess digital tools used in paediatric settings for safety, accuracy and equity.
Identify where digital systems may expose children or exclude vulnerable families.
Plan and deliver telehealth and remote monitoring with clear escalation pathways.
Adapt evidence-based global strategies to local child-health contexts and resources.

cards.title: Digital Paediatric Records
cards.body: Continuity of Care — With Critical Caution

bullets.label: Shared records improve care continuity across teams and settings.
Incorrect weight, copied data or outdated medication details can cause serious harm.
Critical practice: Always verify weight-based
bullets.text: Critical practice: Always verify weight-based medication calculations and allergies at each encounter. Never assume a digital record is current or correct.

cards.title: Telehealth & Remote Monitoring
cards.body: Virtual care extends reach to children with chronic disease and families in rural or underserved areas — but it must be implemented safely.

bullets.label: Define when and how to escalate from virtual to in-person care.
Provide offline or phone-based options for families without reliable internet.
Remote devices must be calibrated, maintained and interpreted in clinical context.

cards.title: Core Concept
cards.body: Privacy & Adolescent Digital Rights

bullets.label: Adolescents have a legal and ethical right to
bullets.text: Adolescents have a legal and ethical right to confidentiality in digital health systems. Nurses must balance safe communication with caregivers against protecting sensitive information.

bullets.label: Key areas requiring special protection include:

cards.title: Global Child Health: The Foundations
cards.body: Improving child health outcomes requires action across multiple domains — adapted to local resources, culture and context.

bullets.label: Immunisation programmes are the cornerstone of preventable disease reduction worldwide.
Addressing malnutrition and micronutrient deficiency across all life stages.
Safe environments and education reduce preventable childhood injuries significantly.
Timely, accessible primary and emergency services save lives at every level of care.

cards.title: Clinical Example
cards.body: Telehealth for Paediatric Diabetes: Equity in Action

bullets.label: A regional service introduces telehealth for
bullets.text: A regional service introduces telehealth for children with diabetes. Recognising that digital access is not equal, service leaders take deliberate steps to prevent new inequalities:

bullets.label: Digital innovation must never widen existing
bullets.text: Digital innovation must never widen existing health inequalities. Nurses advocate for equitable access as part of safe care delivery.

bullets.label: Devices provided to families without tablets or smartphones.
Real-time language support ensures no family is left behind.
In-person options remain available for those without reliable internet.

cards.title: Digital Exclusion & Downtime Planning
cards.body: Review & Adapt

bullets.label: Every digital care pathway must include a
bullets.text: Every digital care pathway must include a manual backup plan. Nurses are responsible for identifying families with limited digital access and ensuring continuity of care when systems fail.

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Section 4 Summary

bullets.label: Always verify critical paediatric data — weight, medications, allergies — in digital systems.
Uphold child and adolescent privacy rights in accordance with law and policy.
Prepare for digital exclusion, limited access and unexpected system downtime.
Apply global evidence thoughtfully within local cultural and resource contexts.
NCLEX Focus: Be prepared for questions on safe
bullets.text: NCLEX Focus: Be prepared for questions on safe digital record use, telehealth escalation, adolescent confidentiality and culturally adapted paediatric care.
